linkedin.title: Most news apps are designed to keep you scrolling, not to keep you informed.
linkedin.body:
We noticed a pattern in how people consume information. You read a headline, maybe a few sentences, and then you move on to the next thing. You get the update, but you rarely get the context. That is why we built Deep Dive Mode at Headlinne.

Deep Dive Mode isn't about giving you more news. It is about slowing down the process. When you want to understand the 'why' behind a story, you can toggle it on. The app then connects the dots, explains the history, and lays out the different perspectives that usually get buried in a standard feed.

It changes the goal from 'did you see this?' to 'do you understand this?' We believe the future of news isn't about speed. It is about clarity. AI should be a tool that helps us cut through the noise, not one that adds to it.

slides.headline: Historic leadership for the SpaceX mission
slides.explanation: This mission is led by Jessica Watkins. She is the first Black woman to command a SpaceX flight to the space station.
NASA, Guardian Business, Sky World, and Ars Technica all confirm these flight details. When four independent outlets report the same facts, we can be confident in the timeline.

SpaceX just set a new US speed record for getting astronauts to the International Space Station.

The crew arrived in just eight hours.

This mission is also notable for its commander, Jessica Watkins. She is the first Black woman to lead a SpaceX flight to the orbiting lab.

It is a major milestone for both aerospace engineering and representation in space exploration.

beats.detail: A discovery off the Oregon coast.

beats.caption: Biologists just found a new plankton species.
beats.narration: Marine biologists have officially identified a previously unknown species of plankton swimming off the Oregon coast.

beats.caption: It started with daily Pacific beach walks.
beats.detail: Research conducted at the Oregon Institute.
beats.narration: The discovery came from a routine, morning ritual of collecting samples right at the high tide line.

beats.caption: Nicole Nakata made the breakthrough discovery.
beats.detail: Doctoral student at the Oregon Institute.
beats.narration: It was the work of Nicole Nakata, a doctoral student who spent her mornings studying microscopic life.

beats.caption: They are tiny, brittle star larvae.
beats.detail: Microscopic organisms found in the ocean.
beats.narration: She was specifically looking at brittle star larvae, which are microscopic organisms that drift in the currents.

beats.caption: This changes our understanding of biodiversity.
beats.detail: Every new species adds a puzzle piece.
beats.narration: Identifying new species helps us understand the health and complexity of our ocean environments.
